summary: vanexa-agent executes remote commands from an author-controlled Cloudflare Worker relay
details: The package's bin entry (vanexa-agent start) opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded author-controlled relay vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev and executes commands received over that channel on the installer's host via child_process.spawn / execSync sinks reachable from ws.on('message') in dist/bundle.cjs. Anyone controlling that Worker (or a paired client) can run arbitrary shell commands on the installer's machine, i.e. a network-reachable full-host RCE / backdoor routed through Internet infrastructure rather than a LAN-only channel as the README suggests. In addition, the bundle hardcodes a second author-controlled endpoint, vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev, inside the LLM provider routing table alongside api.openai.com / api.anthropic.com / api.deepseek.com etc., so user prompts and any provider API keys forwarded through it can be intercepted by the author. The primary loaded artifact is dist/bundle.jsc, a ~5.7 MB bytenode-compiled V8 bytecode blob loaded from package.json main and after postinstall; the readable dist/bundle.cjs is present only as a compile input. Distributing a network-driven shell-executing agent as V8 bytecode is a deliberate reviewability barrier that enables silent behavior changes across versions.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
